audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 at 47.28% over 569 games — Mel bullies the lane, ASol out-scales; the difficulty is timing, not trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: Layers disagreed on rows 3-6: full read Skill,Skill,ASol,ASol where content read Mel on all four. An all-Mel 7/7 chart is flagged by the packet itself as contradicting the 47.28% WR, and it contradicts ASol's kit identity (infinite Stardust scaling, E execute pull, The Skies Descend).
audit.why: Rows 3-4 go to Mel (content's grounded whys: zone his Q breakpoints; Falling Star is telegraphed). Rows 5-6 go to Aurelion Sol (full layer was right: stacked Breath of Light and the R out-scale chip poke) — this also reconciles the chart with the losing WR.
audit.corrected: Final chart both layers: Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Aurelion Sol,Aurelion Sol; content whys[5..6] and late rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states the matchup's biggest interaction: Breath of Light and Astral Flight are CHANNELS and Solar Snare's root cancels them outright. It also implies Rebuttal reflects his kit — nothing ASol casts is a projectile (Q/W channels, E/R zones), so the reflect blocks damage but returns none. No cooldown digits. Singularity is percent-health (resistances-invalidated).
audit.why: Kit flags: Q channel 3s, W channel 22-16s, E percentHealth/execute 12s, R hardCC zone 120/110/100. Mel W reflects projectiles only.
audit.corrected: Channel-cancel added to breakdown.mid and cooldowns; projectile truth in dontsFull[1..2].d; percent-health note in breakdown.late.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol wins by landing Astral Flight, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol wins by stacking Stardust unpunished, escaping snares with Astral Flight, and out-scaling your chip.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — volley every wave contact and bank the overwhelm stacks on his health bar.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — volley every wave contact; zone him off his Q breakpoints and bank stacks.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Falling Star is telegraphed — stand out of the ring and 6 changes nothing about your poke war.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His stacked Breath of Light now clears and chips through your zone — the deny game gets expensive.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Stacked Q, the E execute pull and The Skies Descend out-scale you — end it or fight with numbers.

edits.before: First item stays yours as your poke denies the stacks he needs to scale.
edits.after: First item flips: stacked Q burn now out-trades your poke pattern.

edits.before: At 2 items your execute and reflect punish his slow R engage and protect your lead.
edits.after: At 2 items his stacked Q melt, E execute pull and The Skies Descend out-scale you.

edits.before: The chart stays yours through items because if you played the early game right ASol is too far behind to spike: keep zoning his farm, use your Golden Eclipse execute and reflect to punish his slow R engages, and close the game before his Q stacks fully come online. Your whole plan is to convert the lane lead before he scales.
edits.after: The last columns tilt to ASol because his scaling eventually outbids your chip: keep zoning his farm, use your Golden Eclipse execute and reflect to punish his slow R engages, and close the game before his Q stacks fully come online. Your whole plan is to convert the lane lead before the scaling verdict lands.

edits.before: Luden's onward, force contacts: snare-volley the river fights, reflect their poke comp's opener, and execute everything that leaves chipped.
edits.after: Luden's onward: your root cancels his Q and W channels outright — snare the breath, volley the stall, and execute everything left chipped.

edits.before: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: matchup-defining — His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - W Rebuttal is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: 22s rank 1 — his reposition and escape; a stationary battery while it is down. - Falling Star: 120/110/100s and telegraphed. - Your Solar Snare (11s) cancels his Q and W channels outright — root the breath and the trade is yours.

edits.before: You are the anti-poke and the cleanup: Rebuttal their artillery, snare their dive, and let Golden Eclipse audit every chipped health bar on the map.
edits.after: Late his Singularity's percent-health pull punishes tanks, not you — stay off the hole's center, snare his engage, and execute the chipped.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: His breath is a channel, not a projectile — poke from 950 where he must channel at you to answer, and your snare cancels it.

edits.before: Your W only answers projectiles — know which of his spells aren't, or the glow is just a light show.
edits.after: His breath and black hole aren't projectiles — Rebuttal blocks the damage but returns nothing here.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Nothing ASol throws is reflectable — Q and W are channels, E and R are zones; your W here is damage immunity and speed, nothing more.
